sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Colors, corners and folder scanning
sections.what: Sets which folders Tailwind scans, the dark mode method, and brand, health, and shared color names. Also sets the larger corner sizes, with the card corner marked as the Maate card style.
sections.why: Named colors and corners keep the app visually consistent and let the health status colors carry shared meaning.
sections.watch_out: Styles used in folders not in the scan list will be missing from the final stylesheet.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Shadows, animations and plugin
sections.what: Defines the named shadow styles, two accordion open and close animations, and loads the animation plugin.
sections.why: Shared shadows and animations keep cards and panels looking the same across the app.
sections.watch_out: The plugin is loaded with a require call, so it must be installed or the build fails.

summary: Sets the design system for the web app: brand colors, health status colors, rounded corners, shadows, animations, and which folders Tailwind scans for styles.
purpose: Keeps the look of the app consistent, with named colors and shapes that components can use by name.
why: Named tokens let designers change a color in one place. The comments mark the card radius as the Maate card style.
how: Tailwind reads this file during the build. It finds style class names used in the listed folders and creates only those styles. The file extends the default theme with brand, health, and shared color names, extra corner sizes, shadows, and two accordion animations, then adds the animation plugin.
inputs: The style class names used in code files under pages, components, and app folders.
outputs: The generated stylesheet used by the web app.
risks: Styles used in other folders, such as hooks or lib, will not be generated. Changing a shared color name affects every component using it.
debug: If a style does not appear, check that the file using it is inside one of the scanned folders and that the class name is spelled correctly. If colors look wrong, check the shared color names and the CSS variables they point to.
